source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Green leafhopper (Nephotettix virescens and related species) covers four named species in the deck (N. virescens, N. nigropictus, N. malayanus, N. cincticeps); adults are pale green with a black spot pattern near the wing tips. Direct feeding loss is usually minor, but green leafhopper is economically important mainly as the vector of rice tungro virus disease, with the deck describing increasing tungro-linked damage in recent years in its area. Predators noted include spiders and damselflies feeding on both nymphs and adults. Egg masses are inserted into leaf-sheath tissue and hatch to give several overlapping generations across the season, favored by continuous rice cropping without a break that would interrupt the pest's life cycle.
